message.content: {"caption":"Workflow diagram of a reasoning model that proposes tasks, solves them, and updates jointly from two reward signals.","description":"A process diagram centers on a purple rounded box labeled “Absolute Zero Reasoner.” A coral solid arrow labeled “PROPOSE” leaves the box, rises, and points right to a green “Construct & Estimate” box, decorated with a Python logo. A purple solid arrow labeled “SOLVE” leaves the reasoner below, turns right, and points to a green “Verify” box, also decorated with a Python logo. A white outlined “Task Types” panel sits between the green boxes and the reasoner. Its three examples show Abduction as O = P (unknown), Deduction as unknown = P (I), and Induction as O = unknown (I); the unknown term in each is drawn as a dotted placeholder. A solid connector runs from the panel’s right edge up to a junction on the solid line leaving “Construct & Estimate.” A solid left-pointing arrow labeled “Self-play” runs from the task-types panel back to the reasoner. A coral dashed connection runs from the junction to a peach “Learnability Reward” box. From there, a coral dashed arrow points down to a dark “Joint Update” box. A purple dashed connection runs from “Verify” to a peach “Accuracy Reward” box, and a purple dashed arrow points up from that reward box to “Joint Update.” The legend identifies solid arrows as model input/output and dashed arrows as model reward; a key defines P as Program, I as Input, and O as Output. The Python logos denote Python use in the construction/estimation and verification steps.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
